H41-A.title: NW-tip to nearest N/NNE-trace strain-transfer corridor
H41-A.layers: existing_faults.tif (catalogue geometry) + gdr_qfaults_traces.csv slip_sense; corroboration from lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif band 11 (local lineament strike)
H41-A.physical_signature: Bipartite catalogue geometry: NW-striking dextral trace endpoints connected to the nearest NNE-to-N-striking normal trace, tapered, cut at 200-300 m from the published catalogue
H41-A.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: Faulds, Henry & Hinz (2005) - 'The strike-slip faults end in arrays of ~N-striking normal faults, suggesting that dextral shear diffuses into extension in the Great Basin.' Anderson & Faulds (Emerson Pass, OSTI 1110519) record the type locality INSIDE this footprint: the Pyramid Lake fault terminates and transfers strain to the Lake Range fault. If such a linkage is incompletely mapped, the corridor is exactly where the missing trace belongs.
H41-A.how_it_differs_from_prior_work: Not a catalogue-density multiplier, not a scarp filter, not a learned detector. It is a bipartite geometric construction between two kinematically distinct populations, plus an orientation test. The sibling repository 16GEMSDOE/H18-3a sourced endpoints and junctions from labels.tif as a km-scale prior; this is endpoint-specific, population-pair-specific and 100 m-resolution.
H41-A.status: MEASURED, NOT COMPETITIVE AS A STANDALONE EMISSION. On this repository's strand-level blocked holdout the corridor-only ranker earns credit_per_mass = 0.0000 (fp = mass, tp = 0) in the reference setting - i.e. essentially every corridor pixel is more than 300 m from every held-out catalogue strand. Independently, the sibling session's H41-A candidate, built with different code and a different 20 km block holdout, measured DTI = 0.0000 in all four folds (docs/downloads/holdout.json on main). TWO INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATIONS AGREE. Read together with the orientation audit (below), the correct conclusion is: the corridor is where the catalogue is NOT, which is the hypothesis, not a falsification - and a catalogue-truth holdout cannot test it either way.
H41-A.independent_test: site_control.json: see the 'Transfer-corridor hypothesis' section on validation.html. Geothermal well/spring sites are used as an instrument that does not depend on any fault catalogue.

H42.title: Basin-margin relief x 3DEP scarp x TMI field, density-packed and catalogue-thinned
H42.layers: training_features.tif band 19 (det_elev_slope), band 12 (det_elev) as the relief-position factor, band 3 (tmi_hg); data/external/lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif (USGS 3DEP scarp evidence, public); data/existing_faults.tif only as a 200 m exclusion band
H42.physical_signature: Steep terrain at LOW detrended elevation (range front / basin margin), multiplied by 1 m LiDAR scarp evidence and reduced-to-pole magnetic edge strength; greedy packing at 400 m minimum spacing, then deletion of everything within 200 m of the mapped catalogue
H42.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: Great Basin geothermal systems sit on range-front faults at basin margins; a young surface-expressed scarp in that position is topographically and magnetically visible without being in the published catalogue, and the 200 m thinning removes exactly the pixels whose credit the published catalogue already expresses
H42.difference_from_prior_work: Replaces the H41 corridor geometry (measured 0.0 on the blocked holdout) and the H42 thermal-anchor weightings (measured worse than random on the SGMC instrument). Adds a relief-position factor (1 - det_elev)^1.5 that no earlier field used, and the FIRST field to beat a uniform-random control at equal mass on the 20 km blocked holdout

new_candidates_ranked.layers: GDR 1391 '2m Temperature Probes' (external, free, official) + lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif (scarp corroboration) + gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv temperature field
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: Elongated axis of a shallow thermal anomaly (ridge/valley line of the anomaly grid), i.e. a curvature/ridge transform on the temperature surface, intersected with a lineament
new_candidates_ranked.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: A 2 m anomaly is the most direct surface expression of upflow and was the discovery method at Emerson Pass itself (Anderson & Faulds: 'A thermal anomaly was discovered in Emerson Pass by use of 2 m temperature surveys'). new_candidates_ranked.title: Post-2019 rupture anchors as unmapped-fault evidence (2020 Mw 6.5 Mina / Monte Cristo sequence)
new_candidates_ranked.layers: USGS FDSN event service (external, free, official) -> epicentre trace; corroboration from lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: The spatial envelope and azimuth of a relocated earthquake sequence (a lineament fitted to hypocentres), emitted as a tapered corridor along the rupture azimuth
new_candidates_ranked.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: A fault that ruptured in 2020 is a fault, whether or not it is mapped. The 2020 sequence sits inside this footprint on largely unmapped ground and produced mostly sub-5 cm displacements over zones hundreds of metres wide, so it is unlikely to be preserved in the morphological record that surface-mapping campaigns use. That is precisely the profile of a 'new fault not in the USGS database'.
new_candidates_ranked.how_it_differs_from_prior_work: The family's H33-E was declared data-blocked after earthquake.usgs.gov returned HTTP 000 from a bash sandbox. THIS SESSION VERIFIED THE DATA IS OBTAINABLE through the browsing path (see evidence/seismicity_2020.json and registry/seismicity_2020.csv). No repository in the family has executed this.
new_candidates_ranked.cost: medium (fetch per time window + lineament fit + corridor taper)
new_candidates_ranked.expected: high, and qualitatively different from every catalogue-derived prior: it is an instrument reading, not a map
new_candidates_ranked.viability: VERIFIED OBTAINABLE 2026-10-05. Endpoint https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query returned reviewed network solutions inside the footprint (20 events at M >= 4.6 in the 2020 window). No login, no key, public domain (USGS).
new_candidates_ranked.status: IMPLEMENTED THIS SESSION, MEASURED, AND SHIPPED AS A VARIANT. The 16 reviewed USGS events were fetched (registry/seismicity_2020.csv), fitted to an envelope (azimuth 101.0 deg, minor-axis sigma 1,919.5 m), and turned into a 11,992 px corridor whose pixels ship as the `h41-rupture2020-union` artifact. The measured result is a NEGATIVE for the corridor-as-truth hypothesis and a POSITIVE for the catalogue-gap observation: 0 of 16 epicentres lie within 300 m of any mapped fault and 11 lie beyond 3 km, so the 2020 sequence ruptured ground the published catalogue does not express. It does not, by itself, identify which pixels to emit.

new_candidates_ranked.title: Second-derivative curvature of the gravity family (concealed faults under basin fill)
new_candidates_ranked.layers: training_features.tif bands 5 (isostatic gravity anomaly slope), 11 (vertical gradient), 18 (horizontal gradient), 13 (isostatic gravity anomaly)
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: Sato-style ridge/valley lines of the second derivative (laplacian-of-gaussian) of the isostatic gravity anomaly - i.e. curvature, not gradient magnitude
new_candidates_ranked.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: Gravity senses density contrast through basin fill, so it can express a fault that has NO surface scarp at all. The Gabbs Valley blind-system study lists 'intersecting and terminating gravity gradients, suggesting a complex zone of intersecting northwest- and north-northeast-striking faults' as one of five collocated indicators of a >130 C blind system in this province.
new_candidates_ranked.how_it_differs_from_prior_work: Sibling repositories ran curvature/tilt transforms on the MAGNETIC family (band 6 'tilt angle or total curvature') and on detrended elevation (scarp filters). The gravity family was used as gradients, not as a curvature/ridge-line transform.
new_candidates_ranked.viability: No new data required for the gravity bands IF training_features.tif is placed (see the README limitation). The bands are not mirrored anywhere reachable from this sandbox.

validation_policy: A candidate is only slot-eligible if it is emitted fresh inside every held-out 20 km block, competes at equal mass, and beats both the uniform-random and training-density controls in all four folds (gems41 metric.dti, eroded interiors).

Report every instrument's reading, including the ones that disagree with the selection. The SGMC independent-map instrument over-rewards mass and high terrain; it is published, never used as the selector.
Never tune on the 0.2778 figure; it is user-reported with no organizer receipt.
The blocked holdout's truth is the published catalogue and cannot reward a genuinely new fault - state that limitation wherever a holdout number appears.

H42 addition: a holdout whose truth shares provenance with the candidate prior is self-referential; H42-HO scores only the SGMC residual minus retained-folds under a 3 px isolation guard (this is why line-anchored arms score exactly 0 there, and that 0 must be read as 'un-evaluable', not 'false').

H42 addition: after a preregistered gate fails, no arm, gate, or kernel may be re-tuned on the same instrument; amendment A1 was the single documented fix, made before its corrected results were seen.
